color.$description: Primitives. The only place raw colour values live. Name by role in the palette, not by use.

ink.$description: Darkest brand neutral, used for text

paper.$description: Lightest brand neutral, used for surfaces

mid.$description: Mid neutral for muted text and lines; check contrast on paper

display.$description: Licence must cover the client's uses; record it in the brand book

type.$description: Modular scale. State the ratio in the brand book.

expressive.$description: The expressive layer. Built for the surfaces the brief's expression budget names (covers, heroes, campaigns, packaging, environments) and kept off the ones it does not (forms, tables, data, body copy). Nothing here overrides a contrast rule: expression does not buy a readability exemption. Leave a group empty rather than inventing one.

palette.$description: Extended palette beyond the functional primitives: the colours a campaign may use that a form may not. Each aliases a primitive in `color` or holds its own value, and each says where it is allowed.

1.$description: Expressive colour 1. Say where it is allowed.

texture.$description: Grain, overprint, paper, noise. NEVER behind body text: the lint enforces it. Texture sits behind display type, on covers and on large colour planes.

grain.$description: e.g. a CSS gradient or an asset reference, with its opacity

overprint.$description: Blend behaviour for two inks making a third

shape.$description: The shape library: the brand's own forms, as reusable parts rather than one-off drawings. Name by what the shape is, not where it was first used.

1.$description: Shape 1: what it is, and how it may be scaled or rotated

gradient.$description: Gradients, stated as token stops rather than raw colours. A gradient carrying body text must pass contrast at its worst point, not its average.

depth.$description: Elevation, shadow and dimensional treatment. Depth carries meaning or it is decoration: say what each level means.
